en: Narrow your trips to what's upcoming, what still needs planning, or where you've been.
Adding a booking now asks only what matters for a flight, a stay or a train; everything else waits under More details.
Reservations read by trip day, with your next booking and its reference ready to copy.
Linked places and itinerary stops now show their real names.
Rename an itinerary stop right inside Edit. It stays linked to its place, and one tap brings back the place's own name.
Place search now finds places from this trip, your saved list and past trips the moment you type.
When it's somewhere new, search Google with one tap. Looking for a stay puts hotels first.
Rename stops from your itinerary while keeping their place details and directions. Use the place name again whenever you like.
Archiving a trip now shows a small message with Undo instead of pushing your trips down.
Archived trips keep their cover and sit quietly at the end of your library, one tap from Restore.
Find quick actions in a consistent order: Search, Notifications, Appearance, then Account.
When Memories ends your Home page, its paper background now continues smoothly to the bottom on your phone.
Home now fits your phone without sideways scrolling, even when upcoming trips have long names.
The quick-actions button now disappears cleanly as you scroll down, without leaving a shadow at the top of the screen.
Glance at your city’s weather and one useful temperature in a simpler Home header.
Keep your trip collection tidy by archiving trips. Everything stays safe to browse, and you can restore a trip whenever you need it.
New travel photos favor wide views of the places you’re exploring, with fewer portraits and posed people.
Plan multi-hotel trips with clearer stays, suggested lodging, and checkout days that take you to the right place.
Expenses now show what you spent each day, even after your trip dates change.
A clearer summary shows your budget pace, and one page shows where your money went.
Places and Stay now sit together under the day strip, in All days and in every day.
Stay shows where you’re sleeping, and asks for it when nothing is set yet.
Dropdown options stay readable, with room for longer labels and the selected checkmark.
Browse place categories on mobile without a scrollbar lingering beneath the filters.
Plan each stop by its local clock, without timezone shifts or false timing warnings.
Get matching time suggestions and apply fixes directly from your itinerary.
Stay now offers only places to stay, and any other trip place can be used as one in a tap.
Filter your trip’s places by category, and mark any place as accommodation from its menu.
Rename a day or write its note right where you read them.
Day options now sit on the day’s photo, grouped into planning, moving and view.
Each day now shows its planned time with a simple bar of time at stops against travel.
The day’s route preview follows the roads when they’re known and shows stops that aren’t on the map yet.
Timing notices now name the day needing attention and clear resolved warnings when you link places or travel estimates arrive.
Finish reviewing saved timing changes with Done to clear their notice while keeping unresolved issues visible.
See useful travel details without distracting cache labels or retrieval dates across routes, places, weather, and currency tools.
Resolve timing conflicts with one shared suggestion, then review and apply the connected stops together.
All days no longer stretches wider than your screen when a day or stop has a long title.
Tell the AI Planner where you're staying and your hotel becomes the Stay for those nights, even with more than one stay.
A stay that can't be found on the map is still kept as your own place.
Timing warnings and suggestions now agree, with a quick action to use a valid time and quieter local-time displays.
Review current and suggested times side by side, open each stop, and apply timing suggestions when you’re ready.
Keep your current times, or apply related suggestions together with clear control over what changes.
Expand long stop descriptions without leaving your itinerary, then collapse them to keep your plan easy to scan.
Opening-hours summaries are clearer, without extra checked-date labels.
Editing a stop is quicker: its time, duration and note show as a short list, and each opens only when you change it.
Delete now sits apart from Save, so it is harder to tap by mistake.
Tap a stop or route to follow one leg clearly, even where paths cross or share a road.
Choose routes by name and see their stops, travel time and distance across your day maps.
Link a stop to its location and see travel warnings update without saving it again.
Fill a gap and rainy-day suggestions now leave out places you’re staying.
A stop’s menu is shorter, with Edit at the top.
Each itinerary day is more compact, with its actions grouped in one place and its options tucked behind the “more” button.
Trip-wide stays now live in All days, and the trip overview focuses on the trip rather than repeating the days.
Timing warnings now name the preceding stop and compare both times in the day’s time zone, making overlaps easier to understand.
The move action in timing warnings now shows its proper label.
Each day shows its stops, planned time, travel and distance at a glance, next to its map.
All days keeps its view switch, Places and Stay in one tidy row.
Set one stay for your whole trip, add different stays for selected days, and make day-by-day exceptions when you need them.
Set when you arrive and leave a stay. Days when you move now start at your previous stay and end at your next, for hotels and homes alike.
Stay dates stay within your trip. Your first morning stays open unless you set a starting stay or a booking provides one.
Your trip page and planner now share the same day cards, pinned under the tabs, so moving between them feels like one place.
Each day shows its own forecast under its photo, and All days shows the weather across the whole trip.
Collections are easier to find in Saved, and a new one opens straight onto choosing its places.
Opening a collection now works every time, and its cover shows photos of the places inside.
Review timing changes before moving or swapping stops, and keep your original plan if you cancel.
Enter your own times to resolve conflicts before a move is saved.
Fixed an issue that prevented trips and saved places from loading after the latest update.
Days with photos now show their picture in the Memories journal's day strip.
Long dialogs keep their title and close button at the top and their buttons at the bottom while you scroll.
Saved and Tools pages keep the same heading while they load, so nothing jumps when your places appear.
Search opens straight to the field, with shortcuts into your current trip and your recent searches.
Narrow results by trips, places, bookings, memories or notes, and see the matching words at a glance.
AI trip plans now recognise more places across languages and name variations, with destination countries filled in more reliably.
A trip's tabs now stay pinned on every section as you scroll, and sit flush at the top without rounded corners.
Trips, Saved and Tools now share the same heading style, with clearer one-line descriptions.
Drawers across Trove now open with the same calm, consistent header.
Collections now open on their own page, with their places, filters and options in one place.
The AI Planner is calmer to look at, with fewer choices up front and ideas a tap away.
See which version of Trove you’re using at the bottom of your Profile.
What’s new now shows which version each improvement arrives in.
Keep your brief when you cancel AI planning, ready to edit or try again.
Plan longer trips within your plan’s allowance, with countries filled in more reliably.
See what’s new before you update Trove, with a quick look at the improvements waiting for you.
Trip Mode now shows one moment at a time: where you are, and a clear countdown to your next move.
When it’s time to go, directions come first. Free time suggests nearby places from your trip.
Preview keeps its day and time controls in view, with a slider to scrub through the day.
Today in Trip Mode reads like a timeline, with times down the side and travel time between your stops.
Tap any stop to mark it done, skip it or get directions.
In Preview, step through your trip day by day and drag to change the time.
Today in Trip Mode keeps just what you need on the move, with a quick way to edit the day in the planner.
Log an expense without leaving Trip Mode.
The map’s day drawer now sits neatly above the tab bar and never hides behind Preview.
Enjoy clearer trip tabs on tablets and a quieter day-card strip, with the scrollbar tucked away until you need it.
Tools is now a compact shelf that shows your last currency pair and checklists at a glance.
When a trip is coming up, convert to its currency or add a checklist to it in one tap.
Return to Trips without losing your place or waiting for your library to load again.
Return from your itinerary to the trip overview without waiting for your trip to appear again.
Sign out with a clear transition to the sign-in screen, without flashes of trip data or loading errors.
See what’s new before installing an update, even after reopening Trove.
Refresh an older open tab when another tab has installed the latest update.
Enjoy a quieter update prompt, with what’s new just a tap away and more room to read at your own pace.
Trip places now opens on the day you're planning, with what's nearby first and one clear line about each place.
Saved is now a visual collection with covers, search, and a quick way to add places to your next trip.
Move stops with timing that adjusts around your day while keeping bookings and fixed activities safe.
When a stop cannot fit, see one clear conflict instead of repeated warnings across the day.
Open any trip from its card, with a friendlier Trips introduction and a clearer highlight for your current trip tool.
Currency puts the amount first, offers your next trip's currency in one tap, and shows common price tags at a glance.
Task templates now start from ready-made checklists and show which trips you can add them to before you do.
Choices you add to an AI brief now sit beside your own words, and each one can be switched off with a tap.
Setting a trip up yourself now leads straight back to planning with AI.
Plan a trip with AI from a calmer brief: start from an idea, or add when, who and pace with a tap.
Review your AI plan at a glance, see what Trove picked for you, and adjust the brief to see what changed.
AI plans find more places by their local and alternate names, so fewer stops need locating by hand.
Places you add while planning a day now show up right away in your trip's Places.
Timing warnings now say what they clash with: a booking, the travel to your next stop, or a closing time.
A stop that overlaps one of your bookings is flagged for a check instead of being moved to an unrelated time.
Cafés that also serve meals or drinks are no longer flagged as badly timed when you plan a morning visit.
When there's no photo of the place you're at, Trip Mode now shows a photo of the town you're in instead of a plain tile.
Log what something cost straight from Trip Mode's Now screen, for the stop you're at or anything in between.
Expenses are easier to scan: what you bought and what it cost come first, with the place, your note and the category each on their own line.
Tap anywhere on an expense to open it.
Buttons in every panel and dialog now sit in the same place: Cancel on the left, the main action on the right.
Delete is set apart on its own line, so it's never right beside Save.
Each expense now also shows roughly what it cost in your home currency, right under what you paid.
Filtered day totals now add up correctly.
Stops without a title of their own now show their place's name on Home instead of "Untitled stop".
The tasks row on a stop in Trip Mode is now called "Tasks for this stop", and adding a stop's first task takes one tap.
Moving a stop to another day now places it where its time belongs, instead of at the end of the day.
When a stop is out of time order, the warning now says so plainly.
Editing a memory now looks like your journal: photos as prints, your note in its handwriting, and where and when as simple taps.
Pick where you were from that day's stops, with their times, and choose the day and time in one place.
Adding a stop is clearer: when a place isn't in your trip, searching Google comes first, and the other choices say what they do.
Your trip overview now reads like a journal page: today's place leads, with a postcard of where you are while you travel.
The journey shows the stops behind you and the ones still ahead at a glance.
Your itinerary is calmer: a day's weather, timing and map sit quietly under its photo, so the plan itself comes sooner.
A stop that still needs a location now says so once, and the all-days view shows full day names.
Opening Trove with no connection now takes you straight to the trips you prepared, and into today's trip if you're travelling.
Prepared trips, including each trip's overview, keep opening offline after an app update.
Found a trip you love? Save your own copy from a shared link, pick your dates, and make it yours.
Copies always credit the traveller who planned the original.
The All days page no longer slides sideways, so the bottom bar stays put on trips with a long forecast.
Scrolling lists and day strips now fade softly at the edges, so it's easier to tell when there's more to see.
The bottom bar has clearer icons: a plane for Trips and a pocket knife for Tools.
Scrolling through a day no longer moves your stops by accident. On a phone, press and hold a stop's handle until its ring fills, then drag.
The hour-by-hour weather lines up evenly again, and marks the next day by name where it starts.
Clear night hours in the weather now show a moon instead of a sun.
The currency converter now adds thousands separators as you type, so you can check a long amount at a glance.
The swap button now works every time you tap it.
The arrows on place photos and memories now respond to every tap, wherever on the button you press.
Maps have a new Other places button to show or hide the rest of your trip's places, so you can focus on the day or see what's nearby.
Clear an amount with one tap, and press Return on your keyboard to finish typing. Works in the currency converter, expenses and reservation costs.
Stop cards are calmer: opening hours show just the times, and the move handle sits under the photo where it's harder to grab by accident.
The day strip fades softly as the plan scrolls under it, and long trip names fit neatly in Trip Mode.
Stop cards are easier to scan: the time and opening hours sit in their own chips, your notes read as notes, and warnings fit in one slim strip.
Profile now looks like the rest of Trove, with a clearer heading and your photo up top. The theme switch is gone from here; you can still change it from the menu.
Special hours now only appear when a place's hours that day really differ from its usual week.
When you add or edit an expense, Linked place now lists that day's stops, in alphabetical order.
Home now opens on a full photo of your next trip, with what matters right now set on it.
Trips coming up appear as photo cards you can swipe through.
Search now has its own button at the top of every screen, beside your initials.
Search and other windows now close smoothly, without a flash.
Home's sheet settles flat as you scroll, and past trips get a full-width band of their own.
Your profile photo now appears on the account button at the top of every screen.
Home's sheet keeps its rounded edge until it reaches the top of the screen.
Search opens as a card in the middle of the screen instead of filling it on phones.
Trips now opens on a full photo of your next trip. Swipe it to see the trips after that.
The buttons beneath follow the trip in view, and past journeys span the full page.
Dark mode has a warmer look: a glowing orange accent on deep espresso tones.
Warnings and delete actions use their own yellow and red, so they never look like a main button.
On phones, search opens near the top so the keyboard never covers it.
Search has its own button on Home, Trips, Saved and Tools, and sits first in the quick-actions menu everywhere else.
Your profile photo now fills the account button with no ring around it, and shows on the account button in the quick-actions menu too.
Your profile is now about your travels: the countries you've visited on a world map, your journeys and your favourite moments.
Your details and preferences moved to Settings, one tap away from Edit profile.
Add a short bio and a few travel-style tags in Settings, and they appear on your profile.
Choose one of your Memory photos as your profile's cover.
Your profile map now draws a route from home to everywhere you've been, and lights every country you've visited, even on older trips.
The Edit profile button on your profile is readable again in dark mode.
